'''Travis Marquez''' "'''Bonesaw'''" '''Outlaw''' (born September 18, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played eleven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

==Early life==
Outlaw attended [[Starkville High School]], where he played for the Starkville Yellowjackets high school basketball team. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], he was listed as the No. 7 small forward and the No. 13 player in the nation in 2003.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150128194129/https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Travis-Outlaw-6189 Travis Outlaw – Yahoo! Sports]</ref>

==Professional career==

===Portland Trail Blazers (2003–2010)===
Entering the [[2003 NBA draft]] directly out of high school, Outlaw was a first round selection (23rd pick overall) by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2003.html |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He averaged 8.6 points on 44.2% field goal shooting and 3.2 rebounds per game during his first five years in the NBA.

In the 2005 [[NBA Summer League]], Outlaw averaged 18.7 points and 6.3 rebounds in 35.5 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Portland Trail Blazers 2005 VSL |url=http://vegassummerleague.nba.com/teams.cfm?team=14 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714160854/http://vegassummerleague.nba.com/teams.cfm?team=14 |archive-date=July 14, 2011 |access-date=January 26, 2009}}</ref> The performance earned him First Team All-RVSL honors.  Following the NBA summer league, several teams offered to trade for Outlaw in exchange for a first-round draft pick.  Former Portland Trail Blazers director of player personnel [[Kevin Pritchard]] said that Travis "... [is] going to be with us for a long time. I feel comfortable enough to say he's going to be a special player."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Travis Outlaw biography |url=http://www.bdasports.com/ssp/athletes?bio=28 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204052720/http://bdasports.com/ssp/athletes?bio=28 |archive-date=February 4, 2009 |access-date=January 26, 2009}}</ref>

On April 18, 2007, Outlaw set a new career-high with 36 points against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 18, 2008 |title=Nelson, Warriors return to playoffs for first time since 1994 |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270418022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120713094319/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270418022 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 13, 2012 |access-date=January 26, 2009 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He became a restricted free agent on July 1, 2007, and signed a three-year contract extension on July 17.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Odom |first=Joel |date=July 17, 2007 |title=Blazers re-sign Outlaw to three-year deal. Unfortunately, he suffered a career ending injury |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2007/07/blazers_resign_outlaw_to_three.html |access-date=January 26, 2009 |publisher=OregonLive.com}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2010)===
In February 2010, the Trail Blazers traded Outlaw, [[Steve Blake]] and $1.5 million in cash to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for [[Marcus Camby]].<ref name="quick">{{Cite news |last=Quick |first=Jason |date=February 16, 2010 |title=Blazers-Clipper trade: Deal for Marcus Camby completed, Kevin Pritchard says |work=[[The Oregonian]] |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2010/02/pritchard_trade_for_marcus_cam.html}}</ref>

===New Jersey Nets (2010–2011)===
On July 8, 2010, Outlaw signed a 5-year deal worth $35 million with the [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Meagher | first=Sean | title=Former Trail Blazer Travis Outlaw agrees to deal with Nets | website=oregonlive | date=July 8, 2010 | url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2010/07/travis-outlaw-nets.html | access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref>

On December 15, 2011, the [[New Jersey Nets]] waived Outlaw under the amnesty provision.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2011 |title=NETS Waive Travis Outlaw |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Outlaw_Amnesty_Release_111215.html |access-date=December 18, 2011 |website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2011–2014)===
On December 17, 2011, Outlaw was claimed by the [[Sacramento Kings]] off waivers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 17, 2011 |title=Kings Awarded Travis Outlaw on Waiver Claim |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/outlaw_press_release_2011_12_17.html |access-date=December 18, 2011 |website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

Outlaw's final NBA game ended up being during his tenure with Sacramento, as his final game was on April 16, 2014 in a 99 - 104 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. Outlaw played for 24 and a half minutes off the bench and recorded 15 points, 5 rebounds and 2 assists.

On August 6, 2014, Outlaw was traded, along with [[Quincy Acy]], to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Wayne Ellington]] and [[Jeremy Tyler]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 6, 2014 |title=Knicks Acquire Quincy Acy, Travis Outlaw |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-acquire-quincy-acy-travis-outlaw |access-date=August 6, 2014}}</ref> On October 27, 2014, Outlaw was traded, along with a 2019 second-round draft selection and the option exchange 2018 second-round draft selections, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Arnett Moultrie]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141027-trade Sixers Acquire Future Second-round selections And Travis Outlaw]</ref> He was waived by the 76ers later that day.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141027-roster Sixers Announce 2014-15 Opening Night Roster]</ref>

== Personal life ==
On August 14, 2016, Outlaw was arrested and charged with felony marijuana possession in his hometown of [[Starkville, Mississippi]]. On May 5, 2017, Outlaw pleaded guilty to felony marijuana possession and was sentenced to serve two years of non-adjudicated probation.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Outlaw pleads guilty to felony marijuana charge |work=The Commercial Dispatch |url=http://cdispatch.com/news/article.asp?aid=58059 |access-date=March 28, 2018}}</ref>
